name: regexgroup
algorithm: FindAll of ([a-z]{1,64})=([0-9]+) over a whole 50 MB log, then group 1 of every match, rounds times, summing a million plus each group's length (README.md).

skip.c: no std regex in C (POSIX regex.h is not ISO C, and the MSVC CRT has none)
skip.rust: no std regex in Rust (the regex crate is not std; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the checksum, far below 2^62

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own engine; the checksum (a million per match plus the length of its group 1) checks that both engines found the same matches and groups
notes: Mk Regex.FindAll into an arena Reset per round, then Regex.Group(text, m, 1) per match (the bounded backtracker over the match, std/regex/backtrack.mk); Go regexp FindAllStringSubmatchIndex (its NFA with captures on an input this long).
